items.text:
Fall Semester Course Evaluations

The Office of Academic Assessment announces that course evaluations for all fall semester courses will be completed online. The evaluation period opens Monday, November 11, at 8:00 AM and closes Friday, November 22, at 5:00 PM. Responses are submitted anonymously, and instructors are given summarized results only after final grades have been posted.

Guidelines:
• Evaluations must be submitted through the Student Portal using a campus ID.
• A separate form is required for every course, including laboratory and discussion sections.
• Students who complete all evaluations by the deadline will be entered in a drawing for one of twenty $25 bookstore credits.
• Students who miss the deadline may request a paper form at the Registrar's Office, Room 110, Hartley Hall, for a $10 processing fee. Paper forms cannot be accepted after December 6.
• Written comments are read by department chairs and are considered during annual faculty reviews.

Questions about Portal access should be directed to assessment@westbrook.edu or 555-0142. Technical support is available weekdays from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM in the Lund Learning Commons, Room 204.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the notice?

options.A: To explain how and when students should complete course evaluations
options.B: To describe how written feedback is used in faculty reviews
options.C: To announce the opening of the Student Portal for the fall term
options.D: To outline the procedures for requesting a paper evaluation form

questions.explanation: The notice announces the evaluation period and lists the guidelines students must follow, so its overall purpose is to explain how and when evaluations are completed. Options B and D capture only single bullets, and C misstates the topic.

questions.stem: According to the notice, what happens to students who complete every evaluation by the deadline?

options.A: They receive their final grades one week early.
options.B: They are entered in a drawing for bookstore credits.
options.C: They are excused from the December 6 paper deadline.
options.D: They receive a $10 credit toward processing fees.

questions.explanation: The third bullet states that students who finish all evaluations on time are entered in a drawing for one of twenty $25 bookstore credits. The other options reuse real terms from the notice (grades, December 6, $10) but attach them to the wrong situations.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about written comments submitted in the evaluations?

options.A: They are shared with instructors before grades are posted.
options.B: They are reviewed when a course receives low ratings.
options.C: They may influence decisions about faculty employment.
options.D: They are required for students in laboratory sections.

questions.explanation: The notice says written comments are read by department chairs and considered during annual faculty reviews, which implies they can affect decisions about instructors' jobs. Option A reverses the timing described for results, B is plausible but unstated, and D confuses the rule about lab sections.
